claims.text: Carbon fiber reinforced polymer is a composite comprising carbon fibers and a polymer matrix.
Processed CFRP will provide superior comprehensive performance while maintaining a lightweight structure.
The initial material is CFRP in an unprocessed form.
The proposed processing consists of heat treatment and resin infusion.
Processing is to be performed under controlled temperature and pressure.
The arrangement of carbon fibers within the polymer matrix is the relevant structural mediator.
Heat treatment enhances bonding between the carbon fibers and resin.
Enhanced fiber–resin bonding improves the mechanical properties of CFRP.
Processed CFRP will have higher tensile strength than a standard aluminum alloy.
Processed CFRP will have lower density than a standard aluminum alloy.
A standard aluminum alloy is used as the comparison baseline in similar structural applications.
The proposed comparison measures tensile strength, density, and flexural strength under identical load conditions.
The hypothesis is falsified if processed CFRP fails to exceed aluminum in any one of tensile strength, density performance, or flexural strength.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome specifies higher tensile strength and lower density, but the falsification rule additionally requires CFRP to exceed aluminum in flexural strength, which is not predicted elsewhere.
